Ridu 0.2.0 brings more expressive field configuration, reusable content blocks, and improved authoring workflows while keeping production deployment in one Go binary.

## Highlights

- Define reusable schema-backed blocks and rich-text embeds, with inferred labels and generated Go and TypeScript contracts.
- Configure fields through the unified Go authoring API, including typed dynamic server defaults, primitive text and number lists, and optional live server validation.
- Build custom admin editors with application-local components and versioned plugin authoring contracts.
- Preserve live preview across document navigation and field feedback while saving. Protected fields are excluded from unauthorized filtering, sorting, and distinct queries.
- Reduce repeated operation traversal and value copying, and preserve SQLite data during presentation-only migrations. PostgreSQL schema verification accepts equivalent JSONB default formatting while detecting changed values.
- Keep MongoDB image-variant downloads working when upload metadata has field access rules, while retaining collection authorization and managed metadata validation.
- Generate OpenAPI only when enabled in new projects. The initializer shows native-binary download progress and accepts options after the project directory. Fresh development servers discover framework dependencies before serving the admin, avoiding missing dependency chunks during the first load, and handle cancellation during startup gracefully.
- Build the documentation website from clean dependencies and output in the release workflow. Update vulnerable website dependencies and expand API references and configuration, performance, and REST guides.

## Breaking changes and upgrading

The field configuration API, option terminology, block definitions, admin plugin editor contracts, and immutable store value access have changed. Custom integrations must adopt the current APIs; pre-1 releases do not promise cross-release schema compatibility.

Upgrade the Go module, project-local CLI, framework npm packages, and official plugins together to **0.2.0**. Update your executable config and custom extensions, then run `ridu generate` and review the generated contracts. Review and verify migrations when your model changes, run your application checks, and rehearse deployment against a restored backup before upgrading production.
